name: Judah
overview: Judah is a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem and held the position of second in command of the city, as noted in Nehemiah 11:9. His role signifies a leadership status within the community of Jerusalem during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Judah means 'praised' and is used here as a proper name. This meaning aligns with the positive connotation of his identity in Scripture, as recorded in Nehemiah 11:9.
familyAndRelationships: Judah is explicitly recorded as the father of Hassenuah, according to Nehemiah 11:9. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further details on his family relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Judah's leadership role in Jerusalem reflects his importance in the restored community following the exile. Though from the tribe of Benjamin, his name connects to the broader biblical theme of praise and leadership. The prior references to Judah as a key ancestor in the Messianic line highlight the enduring significance of his lineage and character development within God's redemptive plan.
